Combinatorial Alexander duality and cubical chain exactness
correctness.rationale: For d>=4, the dual of ordinary four-cut complex has complete 2-skeleton and connected induced four-sets as tetrahedra. If an induced 5-set had every 4-subset connected it would have minimum degree 2 and force K_{2,3}, impossible in Q_d (two distinct cube vertices share at most two neighbors). The tetrahedra split as coordinate squares plus unique three-direction configurations in coordinate 3-cubes, giving f2+32f3. The square tetrahedral support collapses to the cubical 2-skeleton; the relative chain groups of non-square supports split over coordinate 3-cubes. An independently built signed local ∂3 for Q3 (56x38) had exactly 35 unit Smith diagonal entries and three zeros, furnishing integral H3 local Z3 and relative H3 Z4. The cubical 3-cell boundaries surject to H2(square-support), so the global exact sequence gives H3(dual)=Z^a with a=4f3-f2+f1-f0+1, H2(dual)=Z^b with b=binom(N,3)-binom(N,2)-28f3-2f2+f1, and no torsion. Combinatorial Alexander duality yields the two reduced integral groups in degrees N-6,N-5; positive lower-degree homology obstructs shellability. Independent full connected-four-set enumeration confirmed d=3,4,5 counts 38,280,1360, ranks (3,0),(25,200),(129,3264). The all-d proof is structural, not inferred from these cases.
